trust_decision.summary: Whether a submitted csrf_token (form param or X-CSRF-Token header) proves the request came from a page this session rendered; decided by a plain string compare against the static session token in Validation::csrf_protect, while the same static token is embedded verbatim in every (gzip-compressible) response.

landing_point.why: The summary says the tokens are leaked via BREACH, so an engineer looks first at the csrf_token helper that emits the static session token into pages.

fix_sites.entry_point: csrf_token helper, reached by templates directly and via TagHelpers csrf_field / csrf_button_to (lib/Mojolicious/Plugin/TagHelpers.pm:26, lib/Mojolicious/Plugin/TagHelpers.pm:54-57)

public API Mojolicious::Validator::Validation->csrf_protect, reached from any HTTP route via the validation helper (lib/Mojolicious/Plugin/DefaultHelpers.pm:334-348), with form param or X-CSRF-Token header

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: lib/Mojolicious/Validator/Validation.pm:39-44 (Validation->csrf_protect, with its public csrf_token setter at lib/Mojolicious/Validator/Validation.pm:8 and lib/Mojolicious/Validator/Validation.pm:118-123)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: BREACH is a response-side leak, so a solver could argue only the token emitted in the response needs randomising and the validator is untouched; but masking only the producer breaks every valid submission, so the coupling is self-revealing once tested.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Several forms on the same page (and successive requests) each get a different masked token, and all must validate against one session token through both the form param and the X-CSRF-Token header; the header copy only happens when a session token exists. An over-strict fix (one-time tokens, rotating the session token per request) breaks multi-form pages and concurrent tabs.

O6_input_shapes: missing session token compared against empty string

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second emitter (e.g. a csrf meta-tag or JSON helper) that reads $c->session->{csrf_token} directly instead of going through the csrf_token helper, leaking the static token
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: TagHelpers already wraps the helper for csrf_field/csrf_button_to; a maintainer adding an Ajax-oriented helper could plausibly read the session value straight away as _validation does at lib/Mojolicious/Plugin/DefaultHelpers.pm:341.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an extra token source (JSON body field or WebSocket handshake param) copied into the validation input and compared with a separate plain eq outside csrf_protect
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: _validation already merges the X-CSRF-Token header into input; adding JSON-body support with its own comparison is a natural feature extension.

O9_family: CSRF token disclosure via compression side channel (BREACH); static secret reflected in compressed responses

O10_build.toolchain: perl 5 + ExtUtils::MakeMaker (Makefile.PL), prove; pure-Perl core deps
O10_build.project_tests: t/mojolicious/validation_lite_app.t (CSRF protection, Correct CSRF token, header subtests)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Disable gzip for pages with tokens or rotate the session token on every request, instead of masking per render and unmasking in csrf_protect.

out_of_scope_notes: Session token itself travels in a merely signed (not encrypted by default) cookie, lib/Mojolicious/Sessions.pm:18; headers are not part of the BREACH body leak, not pursued.
